author: Pontoppidan, 1763
summary: 한국 전역에서 드물게 겨울을 나는 겨울철새로, 앞이 트인 평원에서 지낸다. 깃 색과 무늬가 지역 개체군마다 매우 다양하며, 아래 특징은 한국에 오는 아종의 것이다. 바위나 말뚝, 때로는 나무 위에 앉아 쉬면서 주변의 쥐 같은 먹이를 찾는다. 바닷가 암벽 위나 툰드라 구릉, 나무 위에 둥지를 지으며, 유라시아와 북아메리카의 북극권에서 번식하고 한국, 중국, 일본 등지에서 월동한다.

points.en: broad dark brown terminal tail band

art.subject: Rough-legged Buzzard (Buteo lagopus), adult female-type plumage as typical of birds wintering in Korea (December–February): head creamy white with fine dark streaks; breast whitish-buff with dark streaks; a broad, solid dark brown band across the belly and flanks; upperparts brown, the scapulars and wing coverts broadly edged whitish-buff giving a pale mottled look, the flight feathers darker; a whitish patch at the base of the primaries on the upperwing; underwing whitish with a large black carpal patch, dark wingtips and a dark trailing edge; tail white on the basal half with a broad dark brown band at the tip. Short hooked dark bill with a yellow cere; legs feathered buff to the toes; bare toes yellow.
art.pose: perched on a wooden post in open country, watching the ground for rodents
art.scene: Korean winter open plain with scattered rocks and old wooden posts; no people, buildings or text
views: adult, side view perched on a post: creamy-white head and whitish breast, dark brown belly band, dark brown wings, legs feathered to the toes, white tail with a broad dark brown terminal band
adult in flight seen from above: dark brown upperwing with a whitish patch at the base of the primaries, white uppertail coverts and tail base, broad dark brown band at the tail tip
art.build: Large buzzard, 50–60cm long, slightly bigger and longer-winged than Eastern Buzzard. Rounded head, small hooked bill, and fluffy legs feathered right down to the toes. Long, fairly narrow wings; at rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail fairly long, white at the base. Often hovers on fast-beating wings over open ground and perches on posts, rocks and fence tops; glides on slightly raised wings.
avoid: Do not paint bare yellow legs; the legs are feathered to the toes.
Do not paint a brown, evenly barred tail without a white base — that is Eastern Buzzard (Buteo japonicus).
Do not paint the head dark; it is whitish with fine streaks.
Do not paint a white belly; the dark belly band is a key mark of this plumage.
